risk_countries.name: Iran
risk_countries.note: Trump calls the war 'effectively over', but the blockade tightens and Tehran demands its seven conditions before talks.
risk_countries.details:
Trump said on 9 November, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, that the war is militarily 'effectively over' and further US strikes are 'quite unlikely', while warning the US remains ready. Rubio reported no progress in talks. Iran's security council secretary Rezaei told Washington to stop 'manufacturing fake news' and accept Iran's seven conditions; Tehran says sanctions and the blockade must end before talks.

The blockade is tightening: US aircraft disabled the cargo ship Huda running it off Khor Fakkan on 7 November, and CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate to cut land and Caspian routes. The Guard says two tankers hit mines on an 'unauthorised' route; Reuters could not confirm it, and no ship has been named. A Guard spokesman said Iran's missile range limit 'has been lifted'.

Iran's confrontation is reaching Europe: France blamed the Guard's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit for sabotaging supermarket fridges and seeks warrants for two officials, and the US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat.

risk_countries.name: Israel
risk_countries.note: Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate to form a government; Netanyahu stays caretaker and calls for unity.
risk_countries.details:
President Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on 7 November, after more lawmakers recommended him than Netanyahu. He has 28 days, extendable by 14. The election left Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot's camp at 48 and Arab-majority parties at 19.

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister with full authority over military decisions, including on Iran. He has called for a unity government; Eisenkot's side rejects it in its current form. Herzog says the next government must advance the US Gaza plan, and Trump told Netanyahu to stop obstructing it. Shin Bet reportedly found no evidence of foreign election interference.

Israeli drone strikes continue in southern Lebanon; one person was killed on 4 November.

risk_countries.name: Lebanon
risk_countries.note: More than 300,000 remain displaced; Israeli demolitions and strikes continue in the south, OCHA says.
risk_countries.details:
OCHA said on 30 October that more than 300,000 people displaced since March remain so, that about 970,000 have returned to the south, and that Israeli demolitions, fires and strikes continued that week. A military court charged 13 people over a 780 kg explosives truck seized on the Beirut highway; Hezbollah said the explosives were its own and meant for Israeli forces.

The health ministry's last total this board holds is 4,358 deaths since March, dated 6 September. The board found no Israeli military report of a Hezbollah launch between 29 October and 1 November.

risk_countries.name: USA
risk_countries.note: Trump calls Iran strikes unlikely while enforcing the blockade; mediates Abu Dhabi talks with a wider European agenda.
risk_countries.details:
Trump said on 9 November that the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and new strikes 'quite unlikely', after meeting Qatar's prime minister and Vance; Rubio reported no progress. The blockade is enforced harder: US aircraft disabled the cargo ship Huda off Khor Fakkan on 7 November, and CENTCOM set up Task Force Iron Gate for land routes. The US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat.

On Ukraine, envoys Witkoff and Kushner opened talks with Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on 10 November. Officials describe a Russia-Europe security architecture, a possible NATO-Russia Council revival, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Kyiv.

Trump says he expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; China extended the trade truce to 10 January.

risk_countries.name: China
risk_countries.note: Extended its trade truce with the US to 10 January; Trump says he expects to meet Xi and Putin at APEC.
risk_countries.details:
China extended every measure suspended after September's Washington summit by two months on 9 November: a 24% tariff stays off, and critical-mineral export waivers, port-fee suspensions and unreliable-entity measures are paused to 10 January 2027 (Reuters). Beijing warned it is watching US plans to replace court-struck tariffs with Section 301 duties.

Trump says he expects to meet Xi and Putin at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; China says only that it is in communication about a three-leader meeting.

Lithuania's president confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's office in Vilnius, a change Beijing has demanded since 2021, and Chinese diplomats are expected there. Nvidia's chief executive is under investigation over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy; Trump says Xi may raise it.

risk_countries.name: Taiwan
risk_countries.note: Logged 49 Chinese military sorties in a day, the year's highest, as the Liaoning carrier group drilled in the western Pacific.
risk_countries.details:
Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 sorties by Chinese military aircraft in the 24 hours to 6 am on 3 November, the highest one-day total this year, SCMP reports, while the Liaoning led a strike group in the western Pacific.

This follows Chinese coast-guard patrols off the east coast and near Pratas that Taipei says rehearse a blockade. Taiwan is trimming draft exemptions to add thousands of conscripts.

risk_countries.name: Russia
risk_countries.note: Sat down with Ukraine and US envoys in Abu Dhabi while striking power plants; rejects any European role.
risk_countries.details:
Russia's delegation, led by Vladimir Medinsky and including Sergei Ryabkov, met Ukraine's team with US envoys in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first such talks since February. The Kremlin says Europeans have no role in the talks. Russia still demands the rest of Donetsk, and US officials say sanctions relief and a Russia-Europe security framework are on their agenda.

Before the talks Russia struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv. The IAEA said a drone killed a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, which lost its only external power line for about 10 hours on 8 November; the IAEA did not say who launched it.

Canada sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people tied to Russia's missile industry, cyber actors and crypto enablers. Trump expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen.

risk_countries.name: Saudi Arabia
risk_countries.note: A Houthi attack damaged an Aramco tower in Riyadh and set a pipeline fire near Medina; no casualties reported.
risk_countries.details:
A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh on 8 November damaged an Aramco office tower in the King Abdullah Financial District; Saudi authorities blamed falling shrapnel from interceptions and reported no casualties. The coalition said it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province and a drone. On 9 November an attack on the East-West pipeline in the Medina region caused a limited fire; the energy ministry said operations were unaffected, and missiles fired at Riyadh were intercepted.

No Saudi death from Houthi fire has been reported since 23 October. Houthi-run media say a coalition airstrike in Sanaa province killed at least 40 people on 7 November; the coalition has not commented.

Turkey ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 5 November.

risk_countries.name: UAE
risk_countries.note: Hosts US-mediated Ukraine-Russia working-level talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.
risk_countries.details:
The White House said the US will mediate working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, and the Kremlin confirmed. Abu Dhabi has hosted earlier rounds and prisoner exchanges.

Earlier, its attorney general said the FlyDubai co-pilot planned a suicide attack on Ben Gurion airport and acted alone.

risk_countries.name: Qatar
risk_countries.note: Mediator of a two-step plan: US blockade relief and inspections first, then a Hormuz reopening.
risk_countries.details:
Qatar is the chief mediator between Washington and Tehran. Regional officials told Reuters its bridge plan would have the US lift its blockade and release some frozen funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors, then reopen Hormuz under an Iran-Oman arrangement the US has not approved. Iran is reviewing it.

Qatar's foreign ministry rejected reports that its prime minister said talks had failed, and the prime minister said the US is willing to seek a solution. Trump spoke with the emir, and Hegseth with his Qatari counterpart.

risk_countries.name: Oman
risk_countries.note: Its navy rescued 25 crew from the burning tanker Riti; Musandam waters remain a target zone.
risk_countries.details:
Oman's Maritime Security Centre said its navy rescued 25 crew from the Panama-flagged tanker Riti after it was targeted and caught fire. On 29 October limpet mines hit the tanker Louise 1 about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, on Oman's side of the Strait.

Oman named no attacker. Its waters carry much of the traffic now moving through Hormuz, which leaves it exposed whichever way the talks go.

risk_countries.name: North Korea
risk_countries.note: Fired several missiles on 4 November after denying the Binance theft and ruling out talks with Washington.
risk_countries.details:
South Korea's military said North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the Sea of Japan on 4 November; type and range were not given. Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's attribution of the $6.3 billion Binance theft a provocation and said there would be no talks while US hostility continues.

The launches follow a claimed cluster-warhead test and short-range launches in late October.

risk_countries.name: Pakistan
risk_countries.note: Pledged forces to Saudi Arabia under the activated Mecca pact while fighting the Taliban on its border and halting Iran trade.
risk_countries.details: Pakistan is stretched on three fronts. On 5 October it joined Saudi Arabia and Turkey in activating their Mecca defence pact for the first time, agreeing to provide forces for Saudi Arabia's defence against the Houthis. On its western border, fighting with the Taliban continued after Moscow-format talks ended on 5 October with no statement, and it declared an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. On 17 October it suspended trade with Iran at the Taftan and Gabd crossings, citing security and smuggling, even as it remains a mediator between Washington and Tehran.

risk_countries.name: Vatican
risk_countries.note: Pope Leo XIV rejected Trump's claim that the Holy See supports Iran's nuclear program; he met Secretary Rubio at the Vatican on May 7.
risk_countries.details:
The Vatican's posture is to distance the Holy See from the Trump administration's framing while keeping its diplomatic-venue offer open. Pope Leo XIV's remarks at Castel Gandolfo on May 5 directly rejected Trump's claim that he supports Iran's nuclear program.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met the Pope at the Vatican on May 7. The Holy See's stated framing — 'need to promote peace' — anchors both the meeting and the broader diplomatic offer.

The Vatican's neutral-mediator posture is reputational and procedural; there is no kinetic exposure. Watch-points: any formal Holy See offer to host ceasefire talks; any subsequent papal statement on Iran's enrichment program or the Lebanon framework.

risk_countries.name: Turkey
risk_countries.note: Parliament ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; troop deployments need a separate vote.
risk_countries.details:
Turkey's parliament approved the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on 5 November by 279 votes to 119 (Iran International; The New Arab, citing Anadolu). The pact, signed in August, covers intelligence sharing, military coordination, joint deterrence and defence industry, and treats an attack on one member as an attack on all three. It does not authorise sending Turkish troops, which needs a separate vote, and Ankara says its forces will not take part in offensive operations against the Houthis.

A NATO member is now bound to defend Saudi Arabia, which is under Houthi missile fire. Turkey also began 'Sea of Friendship' naval drills with Egypt on 4 November.

risk_countries.name: India
risk_countries.note: Lost a 15th seafarer near Hormuz when the dhow Al-Jusufi was hit off Oman; called for de-escalation.
risk_countries.details:
An Indian crewman died when the Indian-flagged dhow Al-Jusufi was hit by what the shipping minister called an unidentified aerial object near Limah in Omani waters on 3 November; Oman's coast guard rescued 13. India says 15 Indian seafarers have been killed near Hormuz since March, and six Indians were aboard the Al Mayeda, all safe.

New Delhi called for de-escalation. India also warned earlier that US tariffs on buyers of Russian oil would hurt ties.

risk_countries.name: Egypt
risk_countries.note: Parliament authorised military support for Saudi Arabia on 26 October if Riyadh asks; Sisi limits it to defending Saudi territory.
risk_countries.details:
Egypt has given itself the legal option of a Gulf deployment. On 26 October parliament authorised President Sisi, by the two-thirds majority the constitution requires, to send military support to Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it (Al Jazeera; Euronews). No troop numbers, systems or duration were published. Sisi says Egypt's role is confined to defending Saudi territory and borders, not attacking Yemen.

On 4 October Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan's army leader and Somalia's president declared at El Alamein that Red Sea governance belongs to littoral states, as Ethiopia presses for sea access.

risk_countries.name: Ethiopia
risk_countries.note: Received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets, with four S-400 air-defence systems to follow, the prime minister says.
risk_countries.details: Ethiopia, a BRICS member since January 2024, has taken delivery of a major Russian arms package. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said 12 Su-35 fighter jets arrived a year early and four S-400 air-defence systems will follow (The Moscow Times, Reuters). No value or basing was given. The delivery comes as Ethiopia fights Tigrayan forces again and presses for Red Sea access, which Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia oppose.

risk_countries.name: United Kingdom
risk_countries.note: US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat, the second British base vacated after Fairford.
risk_countries.details:
The US moved refuelling tankers from RAF Mildenhall to Germany and elsewhere on 9 November after a threat from Iran, the Wall Street Journal reported, and raised Mildenhall and Lakenheath to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest protection level. The Ministry of Defence said assets move regularly. It is the second British base the US has vacated, after bombers left RAF Fairford in September following arrests on suspicion of helping Iranian intelligence; Prime Minister Burnham has said that activity was likely coordinated in Iran.

British officials joined European colleagues in Abu Dhabi, meeting Ukraine's delegation outside the three-way talks. RAF Typhoons fly defensive patrols over Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, and MI5 names Russia and Iran as the leading hybrid threats.

risk_countries.name: Iraq
risk_countries.note: Parliament made Asaib Ahl al-Haq's Laith al-Khazali, a US-designated terrorist, a deputy prime minister two weeks after US troops left.
risk_countries.details: Iran-aligned militias are entering Iraq's state. On 15 October parliament approved the remaining cabinet, making Laith al-Khazali of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, whom the US designates a terrorist, one of three deputy prime ministers, Reuters reports. The last US troops left Iraq on 30 September. On 15 October the US Treasury sanctioned an Iraqi bank in a new round against Iran's finances.

risk_countries.name: Kuwait
risk_countries.note: Court sentenced three to death for spying for Iran and Hezbollah and plotting to kill the interior minister; Iran's ambassador summoned.
risk_countries.details:
Kuwait has moved from silence to confrontation with Tehran through its courts. On 26 October a state security court sentenced three men to death for espionage for Iran and Hezbollah and for plotting to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef; the sentences can be appealed (Iran International, citing Kuwait Times and AFP). On 28 October Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over an embassy statement it said interfered in its judiciary.

Kuwait was struck by Iranian missiles and drones in early September; it reported interceptions and no casualties.

risk_countries.name: Jordan
risk_countries.note: Gunmen killed eight at a funeral at a church in Karak; three suspects were arrested after a firefight.
risk_countries.details:
Jordan's most serious attack this autumn came from inside. On 23 October gunmen opened fire at a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, Karak governorate, killing eight and injuring about 40, the health ministry said; earlier official tallies were lower. Three wounded suspects were arrested on 26 October in Al-Jadeeda after a firefight of about three hours. Officials have not named them or any group, and no one has claimed the attack. The King promised the harshest penalties and ordered a review of security procedures.

The attack comes on top of Jordan's exposure to the Iran war: Iranian ballistic missiles were fired at the Al Azraq base in September, in the third such episode, and Jordan published interception counts each time without announcing measures against Iran.

risk_countries.name: Bahrain
risk_countries.note: Condemned Iran over Jordan, days after the Revolutionary Guard threatened tanker crews in Bahraini ports.
risk_countries.details:
Bahrain hosts the United States Fifth Fleet, which makes it structurally exposed in any American-Iranian exchange, and its position sharpened twice this week.

First, the Revolutionary Guard warned the crews of oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to abandon their vessels immediately because they would be targeted. That is the first threat in this war aimed at vessels inside the harbours of Gulf states that are not belligerents. No vessel has been hit in either port, and neither government has announced a closure or a change in port operations.

Second, Bahrain joined Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Egypt in condemning Iran's missile strike on Jordan on 9 September.

The combination is the whole of Manama's problem in miniature: it is the most militarily entangled of the small Gulf states, it has just been threatened directly, and its available response is a statement. Whether the threat to shipping in Gulf ports converts into an actual attack is the single question that would change this entry, and the first observable signs would be a port closure, a war-risk rate move specific to Bahraini calls, or a vessel actually struck at anchor.

risk_countries.name: Libya
risk_countries.note: The government says it dismantled the cell behind drone attacks on energy sites and arrested five, without naming them.
risk_countries.details:
Libya's Government of National Unity announced on 7 September that it had dismantled an organised cell responsible for drone attacks on the country's oil infrastructure and arrested five people, describing a broader interconnected sabotage plot. It did not release the names of those arrested, identify their nationalities beyond a mix of Libyan and foreign, or name any state backer.

That withholding is the notable part. A government announcing a security success normally supplies attribution, and the absence of it leaves this dashboard's standing question — who has been attacking Libyan energy infrastructure — open rather than answered. The National Oil Corporation has not declared force majeure. The claim is carried by a single directory outlet and is published as reported.

risk_countries.name: Japan
risk_countries.note: Demanded Russia return Japan Tobacco's four businesses after Putin placed them under state control.
risk_countries.details:
Putin placed the Russian operations of Japan Tobacco International under state control on 5 November (Euronews; The Moscow Times); Tokyo demanded the return of four businesses. It follows a decree in October seizing several European firms' Russian assets.

Japan's role in the region otherwise centres on Okinawa basing, a debate on a large defence-spending increase, and coordination with the US ahead of APEC.

risk_countries.name: Romania
risk_countries.note: A drone sank the cargo ship Khoryv off Constanta, killing one; President Dan blames Russia's escalation.
risk_countries.details:
Romania's coast is now where the Black Sea war kills sailors. On 23 October the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv sank after a drone strike about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters; one sailor died, nine were rescued and three are missing. President Nicusor Dan said it was 'part of Russia's escalation process in its war in Ukraine'. Reuters counts at least seven cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in two weeks.

Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran drones over Romanian waters near Sulina on 17 October. NATO's council, meeting at Bucharest's request on 20 October, agreed to send more patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea but no new command. Romania has proposed a rotating NATO Black Sea command it would host from 2028.

risk_countries.name: South Korea
risk_countries.note: Reported North Korea's 4 November missile launch from Sondok; Pyongyang rules out talks with Washington.
risk_countries.details:
South Korea's Joint Chiefs said North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the Sea of Japan on 4 November. Kim Yo Jong denied North Korean involvement in the Binance theft and ruled out talks with the US.

Seoul earlier vowed firm retaliation as Pyongyang threatened deployments near the border, and it has pulled embassy staff from Kyiv over a prisoner dispute.

risk_countries.name: Germany
risk_countries.note: Raised its Russian sabotage threat level to 'significant' for the first time and arrested a Ukrainian suspected of spying for Russia.
risk_countries.details: Germany's counter-intelligence cases reached the top of its own system. On 6 October prosecutors arrested August Hanning, a former head of the BND foreign-intelligence service, on suspicion of treasonous espionage for a foreign service they did not name; Süddeutsche Zeitung reports Russia is not involved. On 14 October a Ukrainian ex-officer went on trial in Hamburg as the alleged leader of the 2022 Nord Stream sabotage, which he and Kyiv deny. Two German teenagers were charged in Bulgaria over the 9 October Starlink-site fire.

risk_countries.name: Canada
risk_countries.note: Sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people tied to Russia's missile industry, cyber actors and crypto enablers.
risk_countries.details:
Foreign minister Anita Anand announced new Russia sanctions on 9 November at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, adding 38 entities and 24 individuals linked to Russia's ballistic-missile industry, Russian cyber actors and financial enablers including crypto exchanges.

In September the EU invited Canada to become its first associate member, offering an alliance covering technology, defence industry, energy and critical minerals as Ottawa seeks less dependence on US trade. Canada's Treasury-sanctioned money-exchange firms that moved Iranian funds were named by the US on 6 November.

risk_countries.name: Syria
risk_countries.note: Foreign minister confirms Damascus is discussing joining the Mecca defence pact.
risk_countries.details:
Foreign Minister al-Shaibani confirmed that Syria is discussing whether to join the defence pact of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, giving no conditions or timeline, and said Syria's security is inseparable from Gulf stability. Joining could tie Damascus to the kingdom's war with the Houthis, the New York Times notes.

Jordan said it stopped an armed group trying to enter from Syria.

risk_countries.name: Chad
risk_countries.note: Accused Sudan of an air strike near their shared border that killed twelve at a fuel market; Sudan has not responded.
risk_countries.details:
Chad borders Sudan's Darfur region and has absorbed large numbers of people displaced by that war. On 28 August its government accused Sudan of carrying out an air strike near the shared border, killing twelve people at a fuel market. Sudan has not responded, and no independent verification of responsibility has been published.

The allegation matters because this board has carried Sudan as an internal war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces. A cross-border strike between two states is a different object, and if substantiated it would widen the conflict rather than deepen it. Chad has previously been named in reporting as a transit route for supplies reaching the Rapid Support Forces, which both governments dispute.

The entry opens at a low risk level because the claim rests on one government's statement carried by a single outlet, with no attribution established and no second state confirming it.

risk_countries.name: Venezuela
risk_countries.note: Opposition leader Machado returned from exile; interim president Delcy Rodríguez governs with no election scheduled.
risk_countries.details:
Venezuela is in a transition without an election date. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez has governed since US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January 2026. Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned on 25 October after about ten months in exile, France 24 reports; she had declined to join US-backed reconciliation talks between the government and parts of the opposition, whose first round ended in August without an election date.

On the economy, the Treasury was reported in September to have licensed five international oil companies to operate in Venezuela; the instrument itself has not been read by this board. Washington's posture in the region has hardened toward Cuba, where Rubio has urged citizens to work with the CIA.

risk_countries.name: Ukraine
risk_countries.note: Opened US-mediated talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi as Russia hit power plants and a nuclear-plant worker was killed.
risk_countries.details:
Defence minister Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's delegation at the Abu Dhabi talks, which opened on 10 November with US envoys mediating. Kyiv's agenda is a cessation of hostilities, security guarantees and humanitarian steps; a senior official said it has no particular expectations. Ukraine met European and US officials separately before the session.

Russian forces struck the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv on 9 November. The IAEA said a drone killed a worker at the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant after it lost its only external line for about 10 hours. Bulgaria confirmed six bodies aboard the tanker Wine Trader, hit off Romania on 15 October.

NATO's top commander said in late October that no European-funded PURL deliveries have been delayed.

risk_countries.name: France
risk_countries.note: Blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges; seeks warrants and EU sanctions.
risk_countries.details:
France made Europe's first government attribution of a large Iranian cyber sabotage campaign. Foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the Revolutionary Guard was behind attacks on 11-12 October that raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets. The Paris prosecutor opened a probe into the Guard's Shahid Kaveh unit and requested international arrest warrants for two officials. Barrot said France 'rules nothing out', will summon Iran's ambassador and will seek EU sanctions. Similar suspected attacks on 2 November hit at least nine other European countries, not yet attributed.

On Ukraine, Barrot said European officials would be present at the Abu Dhabi talks and that European security cannot be negotiated with Russia before a ceasefire.

France is one of two European nuclear powers and has pledged forces and air defences to protect Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port.

risk_countries.name: Hungary
risk_countries.note: Expelled ten Russian diplomats two weeks after designating Russia a threat; Moscow promised a harsh reply.
risk_countries.details:
Hungary expelled ten staff of Russia's diplomatic mission on 8 September for activities its foreign minister said were unacceptable under the Vienna Convention, saying the decision protects Hungary's security and sovereignty. Russia's foreign ministry promised a harsh and painful response. It follows Budapest's 26 August instruction designating Russia a threat to Hungary, Europe and the global order.

Under Péter Magyar, in office since May, Hungary has moved from the alliance's most Russia-friendly member to one taking measures its neighbours have not — a datum that runs with, not against, the alliance axis. Ukraine's foreign minister called the expulsion timely and sensible. Carried by a single directory outlet.

risk_countries.name: Poland
risk_countries.note: Sent forces and counter-terrorism police to the Kaliningrad border after warnings of Russian sabotage in early November.
risk_countries.details:
Tusk said border guards saw people with flashlights at the Kaliningrad border just after midnight on 3 November and that forces and equipment were sent; he said Polish and NATO intelligence had warned of sabotage or provocations in early November. Police deployed counter-terrorism units to the Warmian-Masurian and Podlaskie regions.

At home, the constitutional court standoff between Tusk and President Nawrocki continues, and a US basing decision is expected around December.

risk_countries.name: Lithuania
risk_countries.note: President confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's Vilnius office as Chinese diplomats prepare to return.
risk_countries.details:
Lithuania's foreign ministry asked Taiwan in September to change the name of its representative office in Vilnius, and President Nauseda confirmed the talks were coordinated with him. Taiwan's deputy foreign minister said there are no plans to change the name. Chinese diplomats are expected in Lithuania this week to discuss normalising relations; China withdrew its diplomatic staff after the office opened under Taiwan's name in 2021 and imposed trade restrictions.

The US has also pressed Lithuania to let Belarusian potash through Klaipeda despite EU sanctions; Vilnius says the sanctions forbid transit.

chess_players.name: United States
chess_players.goal: Reopen the Strait on American terms while the economic campaign does the rest of the work.
chess_players.move: Calls more Iran strikes unlikely while enforcing the blockade; mediates Abu Dhabi talks with a wider European agenda.
chess_players.details:
Trump says the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and new strikes are 'quite unlikely'; the blockade is enforced harder, with a cargo ship disabled off Khor Fakkan and a task force for land routes. Rubio reports no progress with Iran.

In Abu Dhabi, Witkoff and Kushner opened talks with Russia and Ukraine and floated a Russia-Europe security architecture, possible sanctions relief and NATO-like guarantees for Kyiv. Trump expects to meet Putin and Xi at APEC in Shenzhen. The US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iranian threat.

chess_players.name: China
chess_players.goal: Keep buying Iranian oil and refuse the enforcement architecture, while raising maritime pressure on Taiwan without committing to a campaign.
chess_players.move: Extended the US trade truce to 10 January; Trump expects a three-leader meeting with Xi and Putin at APEC.
chess_players.details: Beijing rolled over every suspended trade measure, including critical-mineral export waivers and port fees, to 10 January 2027, while warning about US Section 301 plans. Trump says he expects to meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on 18-19 November; China says only that talks are under way. Lithuania confirmed talks on renaming Taiwan's Vilnius office.

chess_players.name: Taiwan
chess_players.goal: Hold operational readiness through Balikatan 2026 and post-summit PLA posture window; deepen alignment with Japan and the Philippines
chess_players.move: Recorded 49 Chinese military sorties in a day, its highest this year, as the Liaoning group drilled offshore.
chess_players.details:
Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 sorties in the 24 hours to 6 am on 3 November, with the Liaoning carrier group in the western Pacific, SCMP reports. Taipei says recent coast-guard patrols rehearse a blockade.

A $14 billion US arms package awaits Trump's approval, and Taiwan is trimming draft exemptions.

chess_players.name: Israel
chess_players.goal: Establish a permanent security posture in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza before any framework acquires enforcement, and absorb American objection without paying for it.
chess_players.move: Eisenkot holds the mandate to form a government; Netanyahu remains caretaker with authority over Iran decisions.
chess_players.details: Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate on 7 November; he has 28 days, extendable by 14. Netanyahu stays caretaker, calls for a unity government and keeps authority over military operations. Herzog and Trump want the next government to advance the US Gaza plan.

chess_players.name: Iran
chess_players.goal: Convert control of the Strait into sanctions relief and compensation, with Washington moving first.
chess_players.move: Rejects talk of progress and demands its seven conditions while the Guard claims tanker mines and lifts missile range limits.
chess_players.details: Iran's security council secretary told the US to stop 'manufacturing fake news' about talks and accept Iran's seven conditions; Tehran says sanctions and the blockade must end first. The Guard says two tankers hit mines on an unauthorised route, unconfirmed, and says its missile range limit has been lifted. France blamed the Guard's cyber unit for sabotaging supermarket fridges, and the US moved aircraft from a British base over an Iranian threat.

chess_players.name: Russia
chess_players.goal: Absorb strikes on export infrastructure without acknowledging damage, while keeping the war's economic pressure pointed at Ukraine through winter.
chess_players.move: Opened talks with Ukraine under US mediation while striking power plants and rejecting a European role.
chess_players.details: Medinsky's delegation, including Ryabkov, met Ukraine with US envoys in Abu Dhabi on 10 November. The Kremlin rejects any European role; Moscow still demands the rest of Donetsk while US officials float sanctions relief and a Russia-Europe security framework. Russian forces struck the Trypillia power plant before the talks; a drone killed a worker at the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant.

chess_players.name: Ukraine
chess_players.goal: Convert deep strikes from claimed damage into measurable losses of Russian export revenue and launch capacity.
chess_players.move: Opened talks with Russia under US mediation; seeks a ceasefire and security guarantees as power plants are hit.
chess_players.details: Umerov leads Ukraine's team in Abu Dhabi, seeking a cessation of hostilities, security guarantees and humanitarian steps; Kyiv met European and US officials beforehand. US officials discuss NATO-like guarantees. Russia struck the Trypillia power plant, and a drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant after a 10-hour power loss.

chess_players.name: Pakistan
chess_players.goal: Keep channels to both Washington and Tehran while making the Mecca pact a credible deterrent for Saudi Arabia.
chess_players.move: Backs Saudi Arabia under the activated Mecca pact while squeezed by Taliban border fighting and a halt to Iran trade.
chess_players.details: Islamabad's play is to be indispensable to Riyadh and Washington at once: a Mecca-pact partner, a US-Iran mediator and a counter-terrorism front-line state. The Taliban border and the Iran trade halt show the cost.

chess_players.name: Vatican
chess_players.goal: Distance the Holy See from Trump's framing while keeping diplomatic-venue offer open
chess_players.move: Pope Leo XIV at Castel Gandolfo May 5 rejected Trump's claim he supports Iran's nuclear program; met Rubio May 7 — Vatican cites 'need to promote peace.'

chess_players.name: Saudi Arabia
chess_players.goal: Impose costs on Iran's proxy network without owning the escalation rhetorically or opening a second front in Yemen.
chess_players.move: Absorbing Houthi attacks on Riyadh and a pipeline near Medina with no casualties reported.
chess_players.details: A Houthi attack damaged an Aramco tower in Riyadh on 8 November, and a pipeline in the Medina region caught fire on 9 November; Saudi Arabia said operations were unaffected and reported no casualties. Houthi-run media say a coalition airstrike killed at least 40 people in Sanaa province. Turkey ratified the Mecca defence pact on 5 November.

chess_players.name: UAE
chess_players.goal: Keep the Strait open and stay out of the war, while holding the US relationship without joining an American campaign against Iran.
chess_players.move: Took charge of the FlyDubai investigation days after hosting Netanyahu, keeping the Israel channel open.
chess_players.details:
Abu Dhabi's strategy through this war has been to absorb rather than escalate, and to keep its Israel channel open. Days after hosting Netanyahu, it took charge of the investigation into a FlyDubai co-pilot's attack on the captain of a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight, examining a possible terror link; FlyDubai suspended the route. No group or state has been linked.

The UAE is also rebuilding infrastructure around the Iranian threat, redesigning a planned AI data-centre campus into a dispersed network. Algeria cut diplomatic ties with it on 10 September.

chess_players.name: Qatar
chess_players.goal: Mediate the war toward a settlement without Al Udeid becoming a target.
chess_players.move: Chief mediator of a two-step plan: blockade relief and inspections, then a Hormuz reopening.
chess_players.details: Regional officials told Reuters Qatar's bridge plan has the US lift its blockade and free some funds while Iran admits IAEA inspectors, followed by a Hormuz reopening under an Iran-Oman arrangement. Iran is reviewing it; the White House declined comment. Qatar denies talks failed, and Trump spoke with the emir.

chess_players.name: Turkey
chess_players.goal: Expand its position in post-Assad Syria while keeping its NATO membership and its out-of-alliance commitments from being forced into a single choice.
chess_players.move: Ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; no troop deployment yet.
chess_players.details: Parliament approved the pact on 5 November by 279 to 119. It binds a NATO member to treat an attack on Saudi Arabia or Pakistan as an attack on itself. Sending troops needs a separate vote, and Ankara says it will not join offensive operations against the Houthis.

chess_players.name: Hezbollah / Lebanon
chess_players.goal: Survive the framework’s disarmament clause without a new war.
chess_players.move: Acknowledged a seized 780 kg explosives truck as its own; 13 charged by a Lebanese military court.
chess_players.details: Hezbollah said the explosives on a truck seized this month were its own and meant for Israeli forces in the south. A Lebanese military court charged 13 people, two in custody. The board found no Israeli report of a Hezbollah launch between 29 October and 1 November, while Israeli strikes and demolitions continue.

chess_players.name: North Korea
chess_players.goal: Sustain CRINK operational coordination via arms (artillery shells) and troops to Russia in exchange for tech, energy, and food; preserve ICBM/SLBM ladder as posture-signaling reserve; quiet stretch in May 2026 maintains optionality without provoking US/JK-PH posture firming
chess_players.move: Fired missiles on 4 November and denied the $6.3 billion Binance theft, ruling out talks with Washington.
chess_players.details:
Pyongyang fired several missiles from Sondok toward the Sea of Japan on 4 November. Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's attribution a provocation and ruled out dialogue while US hostility continues.

The launches follow a claimed cluster-warhead test in late October. Kim also inspected a shipyard and called for a faster naval build-up, per South Korean media.

chess_players.name: United Kingdom
chess_players.goal: Lead a broad European and Commonwealth position on the West Bank without getting ahead of Washington on Israel policy.
chess_players.move: Hosts US bases now under heightened Iran-linked threat; joins Europeans in Abu Dhabi outside the core talks.
chess_players.details: The US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat and raised two bases to FPCON Charlie, after leaving RAF Fairford in September. British officials met Ukraine's delegation in Abu Dhabi outside the three-way format. RAF Typhoons patrol over Saudi Arabia.

chess_players.name: Kuwait
chess_players.goal: Stay a basing partner without becoming a belligerent, and avoid making a strike on its own soil into a public quarrel.
chess_players.move: Hosts tanker crews the Revolutionary Guard told to abandon ship or be targeted, after two Iranian strikes on its territory this month.
chess_players.details:
Kuwait's public posture through this war has been minimal. On 31 July its defence ministry said hostile targets were engaged and destroyed; in early September its armed forces reported intercepting two Iranian attacks, with no casualties.

On 8 September the Revolutionary Guard warned tanker crews in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to abandon their vessels because they would be targeted, extending its threats from the Strait into the harbours of non-belligerent partners. This dashboard found no published Kuwaiti response.

The strategy remains to avoid being made a party to the war in public while hosting the forces that are the target. A strike inside a Kuwaiti port would test it directly.

chess_players.name: Jordan
chess_players.goal: Stay inside the American security umbrella without becoming a recurring target of Iranian retaliation.
chess_players.move: Arrests three suspects after gunmen killed eight at a church funeral in Karak.
chess_players.details: Jordan's play is to absorb shocks and publish facts. After gunmen killed eight at a church funeral in Karak on 23 October, security forces arrested three wounded suspects on 26 October after a firefight; no group has been named. It has handled Iranian missile episodes the same way, publishing counts without announcing measures against Iran.

chess_players.name: Bahrain
chess_players.goal: Keep the Fifth Fleet’s home port out of the exchange while the war is fought from its neighbours’ soil.
chess_players.move: Condemned Iran over Jordan while its own ports sit under a Revolutionary Guard threat to tanker crews.
chess_players.details:
Bahrain hosts the United States Fifth Fleet and has spent this war as the quietest of the exposed Gulf states. Two things this week changed what it is managing.

The Revolutionary Guard told crews of oil tankers in Bahraini and Kuwaiti ports to abandon their vessels or be targeted — the first threat in this war against ships inside the harbours of non-belligerent Gulf states. Manama has announced no port closure and no change in operations, and no vessel has been struck.

On 9 September Bahrain joined Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Egypt in condemning Iran's ballistic-missile strike on Jordan. For a government that has avoided naming Tehran throughout, that is a real shift in register, and it arrived only once a partner state's soil was hit rather than when its own shipping was threatened.

Bahrain's room for manoeuvre is the smallest of the Gulf states: it cannot credibly threaten Iran, it cannot distance itself from the American presence it hosts, and its economy runs through the same water everyone is fighting over.

chess_players.name: South Korea
chess_players.goal: Stay out of the Iran war without breaking with Washington, and keep a path open to US-North Korea dialogue.
chess_players.move: Will ask parliament to extend its Cheonghae naval unit toward the Strait of Hormuz.
chess_players.details: South Korea's defence ministry will submit a motion to extend the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit's operating area closer to the Strait of Hormuz, limited to open waters south of Oman, after US criticism of Seoul's support for the war. Parliament, the president and cabinet must approve. A ministry committee also approved a nuclear-powered submarine project (Yonhap, not yet carried by a directory outlet).

theaters.name: China
theaters.status: China extended the US trade truce to 10 January; Trump expects to meet Xi and Putin at APEC in Shenzhen.

theaters.name: Taiwan
theaters.status: Taiwan logged 49 Chinese military sorties in a day, the year's highest, as the Liaoning group drilled in the western Pacific.

theaters.name: Iran
theaters.status: Trump calls more strikes unlikely; US aircraft disabled a blockade runner off Khor Fakkan; Guard tanker claims unconfirmed.

theaters.name: Lebanon
theaters.status: More than 300,000 remain displaced and Israeli strikes and demolitions continue in the south, OCHA says; 13 charged over a Hezbollah explosives truck.

theaters.name: Yemen
theaters.status: A Houthi attack damaged an Aramco tower in Riyadh on 8 November and set a pipeline fire near Medina; no casualties reported.

theaters.name: Ukraine
theaters.status: US-mediated talks with Russia opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 November; Russia struck Trypillia; a Zaporizhzhia plant worker was killed.

theaters.name: Sudan
theaters.status: An army strike on Nyala's market killed at least 102, AFP reports; the UN chief is appalled by drone attacks on civilians.
